+Every job will be represented by a `jm.job`. Any attempt to start a job will result in the
+creation of a `jm.job` instance with an ID, even if the job is completely invalid (i.e. the executable doesn't exist).

+successfully,

+A job is marked as **Running** until it exits. Once it exits, it is marked **Completed**.

+hasn't started) or the job has already exited, I will return an error so the CLI can know a kill wasn't sent. Any

+will be a basic authorization setup with two user roles: a Limited User and Super User. The Limited User
+will have a small amount of cgroup resources allocated to it, and the Super User will have a larger amount.

+cert would include a user ID in the client certificate's Common Name, which could be used to query their authorization
+roles.
+

+directly into

+will require
+a new certificate.

+
+The combined stderr and stdout logs from a job will be streamed to clients in real time. Multiple clients can stream
+logs for the same job concurrently, and all clients will receive all logs from the job, even from before they were
+streaming.
+

+and stdout logs will both be written to this buffer. We will also need a
+channel that continuously sends out new logs as they are generated, which we will call `logChan`. We also will need to
+keep track of all subscribers to the stream, so they can be forwarded logs in real-time. To do that, we will make a set
+of all active subscribers (Go doesn't have sets, but we can use a `map[chan []byte]struct{}`). All data sent

+will be fanned out to the `streamSubscribers`.

+and write all of their outputs to shared buffer as they are generated. Since two goroutines will be writing to the

+concurrently, it will need a lock to prevent conflicts.

+subscriber set. We will then immediately
+send all logs stored in the buffer to that new channel.

+`logChan` and the fan it out to all stream subscribers.

+type Client struct{
+    nextJobId int
+    jobs map[int]*job
+    lock sync.Mutex
+    
+}
+```

+The `Client` is the primary way users will interact with this library.
+
+The jobs will be stored in-memory using a map of Job IDs to `job` instance pointers.

+and then create an implementation for each data source I'd want to support (starting with an `InMemoryJobsRepository`).

+The `jm.Client` will have a private `nextJobId` field which will be incremented when a job is created.

+    ID uuid.Uuid

+allow users to interact with individual jobs more robustly.

+readability.

+- **Rejected**: Marks that a job was not able to start.

+  only ever be **Pending
+  ** for extremely short amounts of time.
+- **Stopped**: Marks that a job was manually stopped.
+

+
+Returns the status of a job. Returns `ErrJobNotFound` if `jobId` does not exist.
+
+### `Client.StartJob(exectuable, args...) (uuid.UUID)`
+
+Creates and starts a new job. Returns the ID of the created job.
+
+### `Client.StopJob(jobId int) (error)`
+
+Stops a job. Returns a `ErrJobNotFound` if the job doesn't exist, and `ErrJobNotRunning` if the job wasn't running.
+
+### `Client.StreamLogs(jobId int) (chan []byte, error)`
+
+Streams a jobs stdout/stderr in one combined stream. Returns `ErrJobNotFound` if job doesn't exist.
+and `ErrJobNotStarted`
+if the job never initialized and therefore has no logs.
+
+### Error types
+
+We will be needing a few custom error types, starting with `ErrJobNotFound`, `ErrJobNotRunning`, and
+`ErrJobNotStarted`.
+
+### Resource Controls
+
+To keep the project simple, resource limits will be arbitrary hardcoded amounts. Since resource limits are applied
+**per job**, each job will need its own `cgroup`. I will be using cgroups v2.
+
+The Limited User will have:
+
+- 25% of 1 CPU core
+- 64 MB of RAM
+- 100MB/s read, 50MB/s write DiskIO
+
+The Super User will have:
+
+- 75% of 1 CPU core
+- 256 MB of RAM
+- 200MB/s read, 100MB/s write DiskIO
